title.narrative: SDG Cities Mohurd-China: Accelerating Capacity Development for Urban Sustainability.

description.narrative:
Project Description
Currently 55% of the world’s population lives in cities and this will grow to 68% by 2050 as 2.5 billion people are added to cities. Urbanization has been accompanied with increased wealth as cities now account for 80% of the global economy. Yet increased wealth has been accompanied by increased inequalities within and between cities, and this has been a significant root cause of civil conflict in recent times. Cities have the opportunity through adequate densities, effective mobility, including non-motorized transport, and green ‘lungs’ to minimize ecological footprints, yet currently churn out 70% of the world’s greenhouse gases and waste. COVID-19 has demonstrated both the vulnerabilities of cities and their economies to pandemic, but also their resilience when planned and managed well.
Their sheer population and growth rate, and their ability to reverse or accelerate the achievement of economic, social and environmental dimensions of sustainability, places cities at the heart of the sustainable development agenda. As has been frequently noted, “the battle for sustainable development will be won or lost in cities.” This critical role of cities to impact global development is recognized in the urban specific Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) – SDG 11: Make Cities and Human Settlements Safe Inclusive Resilient and Sustainable. It is also notable that SDG 11 is the goal with the highest number of linkages to other goals, and that two thirds of all SDG targets have an urban dimension.
The achievement of SDGs rests significantly on cities. City governments have an enormous responsibility to localize SDG achievement and enable all of society to engage in ensuring development impacts that leave no-one or no place behind. There is no greater urgency than now, in the Decade of Action, and in the light of COVID-19 which has stalled development progress in cities, to harness the transformative potential for cities to accelerate the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals and improve quality of life of all urban dwellers by 2030.
City leaders worldwide have embraced this role and have started to report their SDG progress to the UN General Assembly through Voluntary Local Reviews (VLR). The New Urban Agenda (NUA) as well as describing the transformative potential of cities, articulates global consensus on the roles of policy, planning, multi-level governance, finance and infrastructure development as drivers of sustainable urban development. It thus provides a framework to harness the potential of cities to accelerate sustainable development. However, there is an urgent need to implement this framework through a set of local actions that produce tangible SDG results, and to reach a scale that generates global impact. This requires a global movement that joins together unified efforts of local and national government, civil society, academia and private sector: all of society.
UN-Habitat’s SDG Cities Flagship Initiative facilitates global collaborative action to enable cities to localize and accelerate the global achievement of Sustainable Development Goals and improve quality of life. SDG Cities aims to reach 1000 cities and impact 1 billion lives – at least 60% in developing and least developed countries – by offering a systematic way to support cities become sustainable and resilient. Through a partnership approach it accompanies cities and local governments in each step of the localization process – from data, though vision, to planning then project design, financing and implementation. It reinforces this process by strengthening local systems and capacities in the drivers of sustainable urban development - inclusive urban governance, long term urban and territorial planning and municipal finance - as foundations of transformation.
UN-Habitat and China
The collaboration between UN-Habitat and China traces back to the early 1990s, starting from information exchange and expanding to areas on projects, policies, international forums, and other activities. Among all cooperation, the most recent efforts from China revolve around the Global Observance and Chinese Observance of World Cities Day celebration, Shanghai Awards, Shanghai Adapted Index, Shanghai Manual, as well as Sustainable Development Goals Cities Global Conference. Moreover, there are several global initiatives that share linkage on the collaboration between UN-Habitat and China, namely the knowledge exchange in connection with Belt and Road Initiative, South-South Cooperation and China-Africa Cooperation. The most up to date global initiative on Global Development Initiative serves as the potential domain for cooperation.
